The 1827 statute gave legal officers three days to bring the prisoner before the court for a habeas corpus hearing unless they were more than twenty miles away from the court, in which case additional days were granted. The Nauvoo ordinance removed the allotted three days and instead ordered the officers to appear immediately before the court unless the prisoner was housed at the county jail at Carthage, Illinois. In that case, the officers had five days to bring the petitioner before the municipal court. (An Act . . . on Writs of Habeas Corpus, pp. 322–323, sec. 1.)
